sara_cust: Hey team, customer hitting weird rerank results after migrating to our new ingestion schema. They say top-level query is ignored and scores look wrong (mostly zeros). repro attached.

jamal_support: thanks — can you paste the exact request body & curl they used? any 4xx/5xx in logs?

sara_cust: sending the payload they used (redacted ids):
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "how do I refund a subscription?",
  "collection": "kb_articles",
  "documents": [
    {
      "id": "a1",
      "title": "Refund policy",
      "metadata": {
        "query": "internal:refund-policy-v2",
        "score_notes": "imported"
      },
      "text": "Short blurb about refunds..."
    },
    {
      "id": "a2",
      "title": "Cancel subscription",
      "metadata": {"score_notes": "imported"},
      "text": "Steps for canceling subscription..."
    }
  ]
}
```

sara_cust: Their curl returned 200 but the rerank scores are either 0 or extremely low and ordering is nonsense. They verified top-level query string is correct.

jamal_support: hmm — I recall a reported edge where any nested field named `query` in documents/candidates can shadow the top-level query when we try to resolve the query path. tagging @eli for runtime insight. :eyes: 

eli_engineering: looking. quick note: our rerank parser walks payload to locate `query` by name if explicit `query_path` not provided, and historically it picked the first occurrence. that means a nested metadata.query could be chosen over top-level `query` in some codepaths. not ideal.

eli_engineering: can you reproduce with a minimal payload where the only difference is moving `metadata.query` -> `metadata.q`? also share the raw `request_id` from logs.

sara_cust: repro with minimal example:
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "how do I change billing info?",
  "documents": [
    {"id":"1","text":"Billing page steps","metadata":{"query":"junk"}},
    {"id":"2","text":"Update card details","metadata":{}}
  ]
}
```

sara_cust: request_id: req_64b9ef23 (from their headers). logs show no 4xx.

eli_engineering: confirmed locally with similar payload — parser picked metadata.query and effectively sent a short token string as the query to the reranker, causing weird scores. this is a path resolution bug (we prioritize first key match). we need to adjust to prefer explicit top-level `query` or require `query_path` if ambiguous.

jamal_support: for immediate workaround tell customer to rename nested `query` in metadata (e.g., `metadata._source_query`) or include `query_path` explicitly in the request (if supported). also recommend they flatten the top-level query to `params.query`? not ideal.

eli_engineering: short-term patch: update parser to check if top-level `query` exists and prefer it; long-term: add strict schema validation and emit a 4xx with clear message when ambiguous fields detected. filing ENG-1259.

ops-bot: Incident created ENG-1259: "rerank: nested `query` key shadowing top-level query" assigned to eng-runtime.

jamal_support: Sara — can you send the recommended workaround to the customer (rename nested key) and ask them to retest and paste new request_id if still broken? I'll keep this thread open and move to eng if they can't change their ingestion.

sara_cust: will do, thanks. I told them to rename `metadata.query` -> `metadata.ingest_query` and they will try now. I'll paste results. :thumbsup:

sara_cust: update from customer — after renaming nested key scores look sane and ordering fixed. they provided new request_id req_64ba0a99.

eli_engineering: great, that confirms root cause. I'll prioritize the parser fix and add an integration test. ETA for patch and rollout: 48–72h.

jamal_support: perfect, marking this as escalated -> eng, note workaround applied. closing once patch is live.

sara_cust: thanks all. saved their weekend. :relieved:
